explanation.title: content
explanation.text: Draw a product-page visit: address, page, server, data, screen. Explain each step. Imagine the data stops responding: what should the visitor see? Finish with a five-sentence explanation for a beginner.

explanation.title: content
explanation.text: Map six changes to project locations: home heading, reusable product card, photo, shared calculation, mobile app, npm command. Match them to app/, components/, public/, lib/, mobile/ or package.json. Justify all six choices and explain why changing a photo does not require changing a calculation.

explanation.title: content
explanation.text: Write a product page on paper with a heading, paragraph, described image and link using h1, p, img and a. Explain each attribute. Check reading without the image and keyboard navigation. Correct a missing closing tag and explain its effect.

explanation.title: content
explanation.text: Sketch the same product card at 360 px and 1200 px. Label spacing, text size and button position. Add a very long title and larger price. Describe three CSS rules that prevent overflow and one contrast check.

explanation.title: content
explanation.text: Calculate two items at 120 MAD, 30 MAD shipping and a 20 MAD discount. Write a parameterised function. Also consider zero quantity, a discount above the total and a missing value. Build an input → expected result table for all four cases.

explanation.title: content
explanation.text: Design data for three cards: available, sold out and a very long name. List shared props and describe what changes on screen. Explain why three copies of the component would be harder to maintain.

explanation.title: content
explanation.text: Map /, /boutique and /produit/chaussure-test to their likely page files. Explain fixed segments versus [slug]. Add an unknown product URL with expected behaviour and a test. Draw address → parameter → product → page.

explanation.title: content
explanation.text: Write a JSON response with two products. Describe loading, success, empty and server-error screens. For each state, specify what the customer sees and can do. Explain why a completed fetch is not always a success.

explanation.title: content
explanation.text: Create a fictional three-product table with id, name, price and stock. Explain why id stays stable after a rename. Write steps to read one product and reject negative stock. Compare stored data with an outdated screen copy.

explanation.title: content
explanation.text: Build a visitor/customer/admin permissions table for reading a product, reading an order and changing a price. Justify permissions. Describe server rejection even if someone reveals a hidden button. Use fictional identities only.

explanation.title: content
explanation.text: Simulate a valid order, sold-out product and browser-modified price on paper. Specify server checks and expected results. Draw pending → confirmed → shipped → delivered, then place cancellation and explain its stock effect.

explanation.title: content
explanation.text: Draw a timeline where a customer sees success and the server receives the same payment event twice. Mark amount, currency and identifier checks. Write a process-once rule and three expected results. No real payment.

explanation.title: content
explanation.text: Prepare a release checklist for a heading change: local checks, build result, mobile preview and post-release check. Imagine the heading breaks the layout. Explain detection and returning to the previous version. Do not publish for this exercise.

explanation.title: content
explanation.text: Choose a fictional product and trace discovery through post-delivery support. For five stages, connect screen, data and a check. Identify two risks and propose a measurable improvement. Finish with three skills to deepen next.
